newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine c. bank says will not fund 1997 deficit.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine c. bank says will not fund 1997 deficit.

text.p: Ukraine's central bank chief reiterated on Monday the central bank would not provide inflationary credits to the government to cover the projected 1997 budget deficit.
"I am sure that for the first time in Ukraine's history, the deficit will not be covered by the central bank printing money," Viktor Yushchenko told a news conference.
Deputy Prime Minister Viktor Pynzenyk pledged the government would not get the central bank to cover the deficit by printing money when he presented the draft budget to parliament two weeks ago.
The draft budget foresees a deficit of 4.09 billion hryvnias ($2.14 billion) or 3.8 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) -- 2.4 percent by Western calculations.
It foresees 2.09 billion hryvnias coming from foreign credits and 2.00 billion from domestic sources but does not provide any more details.
Yushchenko said it was possible for Ukraine to raise the 2.00 billion hryvnias from its Treasury bill market.
Ukraine recently clarified laws to make the T-bill market more attractive to foreign investors.
But confidence in the market has been shaken by three delays over the past month by the Ministry of Finance in making interest and principal payments.
Pynzenyk has promised this would not happen again.
Yushchenko said if the central bank does not print money, annual inflation in 1997 could be lowered to the 25 percent projected in the draft budget, compared to 40-48 percent projected for this year.
"An inflation rate of 25 percent would allow real growth and, for the first time in Ukraine's history, yearly growth in GDP of 1.5 percent," he said.

Ukraine's economy has contracted constantly since it became independent when the Soviet Union fell apart in 1991. GDP in the first six months of this year was 8.7 percent lower than a year earlier, and fell 11.8 percent in the whole of 1995.
